transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-26 16:00 PDT — Duration 42m. Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Mark (Northgate Sec Eng), Lina (IT Ops), Jordan (Product).

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining the weekly POC sync. Can we do quick roll call?
[00:08] Mark: Mark here.
[00:10] Lina: Lina here.
[00:12] Jordan: Jordan here.
[00:14] Alex: Great. Priya from Redwood is on the line too. Priya, quick status from infra side?
[00:22] Priya: Yeah, hi. We finished the initial ingest and KV cache tuning from last week, so latency looks better on small sequences. We'll share updated perf numbers after the bench run. Today we want to focus on the security items you flagged — SSO, audit logs, retention — and make sure the test plan is aligned.
[00:40] Mark: Perfect. Our security team basically needs to validate SAML integration with Okta, confirm audit log schema and retention options, and see SOC 2 artifacts. Also want a clear statement on what data Redwood persists during hosted inference, encryption key management — you know, KMS, HSM — and options for private deployment if needed.
[01:05] Alex: Totally. Quick overview: for the POC we're running on Redwood hosted but with isolated tenant configs. We can also spin up a dedicated pool if you want physical isolation. For data persistence, by default request logs are retained for 30 days but we can configure that per contract; we'll send the retention config options.
[01:28] Lina: When you say "request logs" — does that include the full prompt and response or just metadata? We need to know because of PII concerns.
[01:36] Priya: Good question. The default audit logs include request IDs, timestamps, model/version, latency, and token counts. By default we also capture the full request payload for troubleshooting during the POC, but that can be masked or disabled. We have a configuration flag to redact PII and to only store hashes of inputs. We'll send examples.
[02:02] Mark: Okay, I'd like an explicit option to never persist full request payloads in hosted mode; we prefer redaction during the POC. If you need sample data to test redaction, we'll provide a redacted example.
[02:15] Priya: That's doable. We'll put together a how-to for configuring redaction and show the change in the bench run.
[02:22] Jordan: On the SOC2 front, are you type II? We requested the report in the form we can share with procurement.
[02:28] Alex: Yes, Redwood has SOC 2 Type II as of last quarter. I'll attach the report and a short pen-test summary. Note that some items in the pen test are redacted for vendor confidentiality — we can provide the summary-level findings.
[02:41] Mark: Good. Also, on encryption — do you support customer-managed keys? We need to know if KMS integration is possible in hosted deployments or only for private/on-prem.
[02:51] Priya: For hosted we support customer-managed keys via a KMS integration — AWS KMS or customer HSM via our key-wrapping workflow. For private/VPC you of course have full key control. We'll document the flow and the levels of separation.
[03:12] Lina: For audit logs, what's the export format? We want to ingest into our Splunk instance.
[03:17] Priya: We export logs as JSON and can stream to your SIEM via syslog or S3 exports. We'll include an example JSON schema and a sample export.
[03:27] Mark: What's the retention policy, is it configurable on a per-tenant basis?
[03:31] Alex: Yes, retention is configurable. Defaults are 30 days for request payloads and 365 days for aggregated billing/usage metrics, but contractual terms can change those windows or enable auto-export to your storage for longer retention.
[03:45] Jordan: If we export to our S3, are logs encrypted with our KMS?
[03:50] Priya: Yes, when exporting to your S3 we can use your bucket permissions and your KMS key for server-side encryption.
[03:57] Mark: Good. A couple more items — audit trail integrity: can you provide immutable logs or append-only write patterns with tamper evidence?
[04:07] Priya: We support write-once S3 objects with checksums and can provide signed digests of logs on a periodic basis for tamper evidence. For dedicated/private we can enable stricter controls.
[04:18] Mark: OK. Next SSO. We're using Okta; we want SAML-based SSO and SCIM user provisioning for RBAC. Any blockers?
[04:27] Alex: No blockers. We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. For the POC we can do SAML only and then add SCIM if you want full lifecycle provisioning.
[04:36] Lina: We prefer SCIM so we don't have to manage users manually. Is SCIM supported in hosted?
[04:41] Priya: Yes, SCIM is supported in hosted. It can be enabled per-tenant. For the POC we can set up a small group and demonstrate RBAC roles.
[04:50] Mark: What's the RBAC model look like? We need separation between admin, ops, and read-only audit viewers.
[04:56] Priya: Roles are configurable — Admin, DevOps/SE, Viewer, and we can add custom roles mapped to SCIM groups. We'll share the RBAC docs.
[05:05] Jordan: Any latency or token leak concerns when SSO redirects happen? I'm trying to think of timing windows where a session might expose data.
[05:12] Priya: No sensitive tokens are written to logs; session tokens are short-lived and stored server-side. The redirect flow uses standard SAML flows. We'll share sequence diagrams.
[05:21] Mark: On incident response, what's Redwood's SLA for incident notification? We need 24/7 pager for sev1s for production, but for POC a normal email notification is fine.
[05:30] Alex: For POC we'll do email; enterprise SLAs include 24/7 pager and escalation paths. We'll include our incident response playbook excerpt.
[05:38] Lina: A question about model artifacts: do you keep a copy of model weights or any model training data?
[05:44] Priya: We do not keep customer training data. For hosted we run inference on models you select from our catalog; model weights are maintained by Redwood where applicable for open models, but we do not persist customer-provided training datasets.
[05:58] Mark: Great. Now about private deployment — what of the security features are different? E.g., audit logs staying in-customer VPC?
[06:05] Priya: In private mode all logs and telemetry can be routed to your VPC and stored exclusively in your environment — so you can meet stricter residency and egress rules.
[06:14] Alex: And we can configure HSM-backed keys inside your VPC.
[06:18] Mark: Good. A small nit — the pen-test summary you provide, does it include CVSS scores?
[06:24] Alex: Yes, summary includes CVSS and remediation status. Full reports are redacted as needed.
[06:30] Jordan: OK. Any blockers from our side for the next steps?
[06:34] Mark: We need the SOC2 and the log schema. We'll spin up an Okta test user and share SAML metadata. Also want to validate that the PII redaction works.
[06:45] Priya: For PII redaction: we have server-side redaction rules and a hashing option. We'll run a demo in the bench run to show that redaction is applied end-to-end.
[06:56] Alex: We'll also provide sample curl commands and a small troubleshooting checklist so you can verify that the SSO and SCIM flows are working.
[07:05] Lina: For the bench run, what traffic profile do you need? We plan to send 10k calls with typical prompt sizes of 200 tokens each. Does that capture the profile?
[07:14] Priya: Yes, that's perfect. We'll run that on a dedicated pool with KV cache on for realistic performance numbers; we'll capture latency percentiles and cost estimates.
[07:25] Mark: If the bench exposes any data, will it be removed after the test?
[07:29] Alex: Yes we can purge test logs on request. We'll include a purge script and a retention change to zero days for ephemeral test data.
[07:37] Jordan: Anything else on compliance? GDPR / data residency?
[07:41] Priya: For EU data we can pin region and Residency. For the POC if you want EU-only storage we can route to our EU region and use the dedicated S3 export so logs never leave region.
[07:54] Mark: Ok, final check. Are we able to get a sample audit log and the RBAC mapping doc today?
[07:59] Priya: I'll send audit log sample and RBAC mapping today, Alex will attach SOC2 and pen-test by Friday.
[08:07] Alex: Yep, I'll upload by Friday EOD.
[08:10] Mark: Great. We'll create the Okta test user and share metadata by Monday.
[08:14] Jordan: I'll coordinate legal review timeline with procurement and get back to you.
[08:18] Alex: Awesome. Let's recap next steps.
[08:22] Priya: Recap: Redwood sends SOC2 + pen-test (Alex), audit log samples and RBAC docs (Priya), provide retention and KMS integration docs, schedule bench run (Priya/Alex). Customer provides Okta metadata, sample redacted dataset, and legal timeline.
[08:37] Mark: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[08:40] Alex: Thanks all. We'll follow up in writing with links.

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings but preserves speaker turns and timestamps. Links shared: SOC2_report_link (placeholder), audit-log-sample.json (placeholder), RBAC_mapping.xlsx (placeholder).
